author.name: Efficiency Emilia
author.role: Uses deep domain knowledge to define business goals, objectives, and KPIs. Aligns ML features with overarching product strategy and organizational roadmaps. Evaluates system performance, operational capability, and project costs.

challenge.name: The Committed Pallets
challenge.description: A supplier has confirmed a bulk order for a middle aisle promotion that ships next week, leaving no room for model error. #requirements_reuben# insists the acceptance criteria must be fully governed to guarantee the allocation logic is auditable before the trucks leave. #reliability_ruth# argues the criteria are sufficient as manual checks because the physical stock is already committed and the team needs to ship the feature immediately to handle the live orders.

output.content: The promotion week cost is the primary factor in our decision here. I am prepared to accept a lower level of cost tracking for this specific release. If we drop the detailed audit trail for the allocation logic, we save significant development time and reduce the project budget. That reduction in spend allows us to move the feature live immediately. I value the faster deployment and the lower upfront cost more than the granular visibility into the allocation expenses for this single cycle. The physical stock is already committed, so the financial risk is fixed regardless of how we track the internal logic costs.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly states they are prepared to accept a loss in cost tracking granularity in exchange for faster deployment and lower upfront costs.
